Note::TexAccessor::labels¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::labels() const

Extract Authored Cross-Reference Anchors¶

labels() extracts the required argument of every complete \label{...} call from each Text cell. Tokens contain the argument body, not the command or outer braces. This is the direct inventory operation for discovering the anchors a document defines before checking references, renaming keys, or constructing a document-level index.

Matching is exact and boundary aware. \labeled{...} is a different control word and does not match; a doubled backslash marks an escaped command boundary and does not begin a label call. Horizontal whitespace between \label and its required argument is accepted. The argument scanner balances nested braces, so \label{eq:{energy}} contributes eq:{energy} rather than stopping at the inner closing brace. An incomplete argument contributes nothing.

This is intentionally lexical. It does not validate whether a key is unique, whether a matching \ref exists, or whether TeX would execute the command in the surrounding context. Duplicate label bodies remain duplicate tokens and source order is stable. Use refs() for reference-use extraction and compare the two inventories at the document layer when unresolved or duplicate anchors matter.

The returned TokenBatch owns one flat Text Note plus Int64 offsets. The offset range [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]) identifies tokens from receiver cell i, including cells with none. Receiver rank is represented by row-major lane order rather than imposed on the ragged token Note. Undefined input returns undefined tokens with offsets [0]; defined non-Text input is rejected.

Runtime is linear in source bytes plus copied label-body bytes. No TeX engine, filesystem access, or document tree is involved.

Example 1: Exact Commands And Balanced Bodies¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\label{eq:{energy}} \labeled{no})",
    R"(\\label{escaped} \label {sec:intro})", R"(\label{unfinished)"});
const auto result = source.tex().labels();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["eq:{energy}", "sec:intro"]

The nested braces remain part of the first key. The longer command name, escaped command, and unfinished body produce no false tokens.

Example 2: Preserve Per-Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 1, 2, 2]

The first two cells each own one key; the malformed third cell owns an empty range.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().labels();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().labels();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "labels Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
labels Int64: rejected
